claims.text: Often comes with low potassium and/or low calcium, and their ECG features
claims.quote: Patients with hypomagnesaemia often have concurrent hypokalaemia and/or hypocalcaemia and associated ECG features of these conditions.

claims.text: Causes (mechanism and diagnoses) Causes: inadequate magnesium intake and absorption, or increased excretion due to hypercalcemia or medications such as furosemide
claims.quote: Causes include inadequate magnesium intake and absorption or increased excretion due to hypercalcemia or medications such as furosemide.

claims.text: May occur with: alcohol use disorder, uncontrolled diabetes, hypercalcemia, or loop diuretics
claims.quote: Hypomagnesemia may occur in patients with alcohol use disorder, uncontrolled diabetes, or hypercalcemia or in patients taking loop diuretics.

claims.text: Link with low potassium: largely shared causes (diuretics, diarrhea), but low magnesium itself may also increase renal potassium losses
claims.quote: Hypomagnesemia is a common correlate of hypokalemia. Much of this correlation is attributable to common causes (ie, diuretics, diarrhea), but hypomagnesemia itself may also result in increased renal potassium losses.

claims.text: Symptoms Often due to the accompanying low potassium and low calcium: lethargy, tremor, tetany, seizures, and arrhythmias
claims.quote: Clinical features are often due to accompanying hypokalemia and hypocalcemia and include lethargy, tremor, tetany, seizures, and arrhythmias.

claims.text: Anorexia, nausea, vomiting, lethargy, weakness, personality change, tetany (e.g., positive Trousseau or Chvostek sign, spontaneous carpopedal spasm, hyperreflexia), tremor, and muscle fasciculations
claims.quote: Symptoms include anorexia, nausea, vomiting, lethargy, weakness, personality change, tetany (eg, positive Trousseau or Chvostek sign, spontaneous carpopedal spasm, hyperreflexia), tremor, and muscle fasciculations.

claims.text: Treatment Treat with magnesium salts when the deficiency is symptomatic or magnesium is persistently < 1.25 mg/dL
claims.quote: Treat with magnesium salts when magnesium deficiency is symptomatic or magnesium concentration is persistently < 1.25 mg/dL (< 0.50 mmol/L).

claims.text: Oral magnesium unless there are seizures or other severe symptoms; then magnesium sulfate 2 to 4 g IV over 5 to 10 minutes
claims.quote: Give oral magnesium salts unless patients have seizures or other severe symptoms, in which case, give 2 to 4 g of magnesium sulfate IV over 5 to 10 minutes.

claims.text: Torsades: a rapid IV bolus of magnesium 2 g is a standard emergency treatment
claims.quote: A rapid IV bolus of magnesium 2g is a standard emergency treatment for torsades de pointes

claims.text: Correcting magnesium to > 1.0 mmol/L together with potassium to > 4.0 mmol/L is often effective in suppressing ectopy and supraventricular tachyarrhythmias
claims.quote: Correction of serum magnesium to > 1.0 mmol/L, with concurrent correction of serum potassium to > 4.0 mmol/L, is often effective in suppressing ectopy and supraventricular tachyarrhythmias
